name: Irish Prison Service
text_head:
What is Freedom of Information?  
The Freedom of Information Act came into effect on 21 April, 1998. This Act gives you the right to 
access records held by Government departments and certain public bodies.  
What can you ask for?  
You can ask for the following records held by Government departments or certain public bodies: 
 
any records relating to you personally, whenever created  
 
all other records created after 21 April, 1998  
Procedure for accessing records  
To access a record you must apply in writing to the Information Access Officer, Information Unit 
(FOI) Irish Prison Service, IDA Business Park, Ballinalee Road, Longford, Co Longford, stating that the 
request is made under the Freedom of Information Act clearly identifying the records that you seek. 
If you are seeking personal records, you should include photographic identification. Should you need 
assist in making your request, you can contact datarequest@irishprisons.ie or alternatively ring 043 
3335100 / 3335377.  
Processing of applications  
You will receive an acknowledgement of your application within 10 working days. A decision on your 
application will normally be made within 20 working days. If your request is refused you will be given 
reasons for the refusal.  
Can you appeal against the decision?  
Yes. If you are not satisfied with the decision regarding your FOI request you may ask the Irish Prison 
Service for an "internal review" of that decision. A more senior officer will review your application. 
You will be told the result of this review within 15 working days If you are unhappy with the 
outcome of the "internal review" an appeal, in writing, may be made directly to the Information 
Commissioner at the following address:

1. WHAT IS AIE? 
 
The European Communities (Access to Information on the Environment) Regulations 2007 came into force on 1 
May 2007 and the European Communities (Access to Information on the Environment) (Amendment) 
Regulations 2011 came into force on 23 December 2011.  Both pieces of legislation are to be read together and 
construed as one and are referred to as the European Communities (Access to Information on the Environment) 
Regulations 2007 to 2014. 
2. HOW  DO  I MAKE A REQUEST FOR ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON THE ENVIRONMENT (AN AIE REQUEST) TO 
CRAWFORD ART GALLERY 
If you wish to seek access to information on the environment under the AIE regulations, you will need to: 
• 
Make your request in writing or via email. 
 
• 
Indicate that the information is being sought under the AIE regulations. 
 
• 
Be as clear and specific as possible in making your request and provide as much information as 
possible to enable Crawford Art Gallery to identify the records that you require. 
• 
You don't need to state the reason why you are making the request. 
 
If you would like to receive access to the information/records requested in a particular format, (e.g. 
photocopies, electronically etc.), please mention this when submitting your request. 
Include a daytime telephone number or email address and your postal address to help us to contact you if 
any queries arise in relation to your request. 
 
Requests should be posted to:  
The FOI/AIE Officer

Cork 
Alternatively, requests can be emailed foi@crawfordartgallery.ie

elements of the environment

environmental agreements, and activities affecting or likely to affect the elements and factors

activities

relevant, conditions of human life, cultural sites and built structures that may be affected by the 
elements of the environment

from public authorities. Under these regulations, information relating to the environment

authorities are required to deal with requests.

County Councils were established under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1898. The first meeting of King’s (Offaly)

grouped together under the City and County Management Act 1940.  At the May Monthly Council Meeting in 1981 the 
members supported a motion that the two counties should cease to be grouped in accordance with the provisions of 
Section 13 of the City and County Management (Amendment) Act 1955. Since 2001, Offaly County Council has had its 
headquarters at Áras an Chontae Charleville Road, Tullamore.

services to the citizens of Offaly as well as a representational body for the people of Offaly. Local Government in Ireland 
operates jointly through directly elected representatives and full time executives headed by the Chief Executive, 
(formerly County Manager). 
Ms. Anna Marie Delaney was appointed Chief Executive to Offaly County Council in February 2016.
